questions.text: Before doing something unfamiliar, what do you do first?

options.text: Recruit a friend for moral support

questions.text: It is 11 p.m. What are you most likely doing?

options.text: Patrolling the comments on trending posts

questions.text: The group chat goes quiet. You…

options.text: Send a meme to rescue the mood
Review the chat to work out why
Quietly go buy a bottle of water

questions.text: You get a task due in a week. You…

options.text: Save your energy for the last two days
Build a tool to automate it next time
Finish it, then go offline all evening

questions.text: Which line sounds most like you?

options.text: A good plan is half the job
If it can be automated, automate it
Get the mood right and the rest follows
Find a quiet spot and let your mind wander
Catch up on every bit of gossip

D1.name: Spreadsheet Oracle
D1.tagline: Your good fortune has a spreadsheet.
D1.desc: You check ratings, horoscopes and sleep stats before making a decision. A good mood is clearly the result of exactly 7 hours and 42 minutes of sleep. You are not superstitious. You just think nobody has gathered enough data on luck.
D1.pro: Fast decisions. The spreadsheet already voted.
D1.habit: Keeping a sheet for everything, including which detergent improves your mood.
D1.share: I got Spreadsheet Oracle. My luck has been entered into a spreadsheet.

D2.name: Strategic Slacker
D2.tagline: Making less effort takes serious effort.
D2.desc: Your meeting notes are secretly a shopping list. Your finest work happens the day before a deadline. You firmly believe that if a task can wait until tomorrow, there is a chance it will disappear by then.
D2.pro: Terrifying efficiency when it finally matters.
D2.habit: Ranking overdue tasks by how long until something catches fire.
D2.share: I got Strategic Slacker. This is paid research into human behavior.

D3.name: Unofficial Hype Crew
D3.tagline: Where there is awkward silence, there is you.
D3.desc: Three quiet minutes in a group chat feel like an emergency. You deploy a meme, then a terrible joke, then another meme. You are not necessarily outgoing. You just refuse to let silence win.
D3.habit: Sorting hundreds of memes by icebreaker strength.
D3.share: I got Unofficial Hype Crew. Awkward silence is my workplace injury.

D4.name: Professional Plan Maker
D4.tagline: The trip is next month. The itinerary is 47 pages.
D4.desc: Annual goals, weekend flowcharts, a better shower routine: everything deserves a plan. Execution is a separate hobby. Your completion rate is questionable, but your to-do lists belong in a design museum.
D4.pro: Always prepared with Plans B and C.
D4.habit: Scheduling time to stop making plans.
D4.share: I got Professional Plan Maker. Execution can wait; the plan must be perfect.

D5.name: Convenience Store Philosopher
D5.tagline: Big thoughts between the snack aisles.
D5.desc: You enter for water and leave with a theory about loneliness. Two-for-one deals raise existential questions. A steaming bowl of noodles becomes a metaphor for life. You never write it down, but it feels publishable.
D5.pro: Turning an ordinary moment into a surprisingly good metaphor.
D5.habit: Naming moods after products: today is iced canned coffee.
D5.share: I got Convenience Store Philosopher. Deep thoughts, aisle three.

D6.name: Untamed Inventor
D6.tagline: Eight hours of coding to save five minutes.
D6.desc: Manually sorting a table? Unacceptable. Choosing lunch? Obviously it needs a custom roulette app. The solution costs more effort than the problem, but future you will thank you. Probably. If you ever use it again.
D6.pro: Learning fast and actually building things.
D6.habit: Reengineering the lights and curtains at least three times.
D6.share: I got Untamed Inventor. Five hours to save five minutes. Worth it.

D7.name: Chief Bystander
D7.tagline: First on the scene. Never in the story.
D7.desc: When a story starts trending, you already have the timeline. Friends ask you to settle disputes because you remember their argument from three years ago. You do not create the news. You just have the receipts.
D7.pro: Always informed, always ready with a conversation starter.
D7.habit: Filing screenshots with dates, titles and suspiciously useful categories.
D7.share: I got Chief Bystander. I know everything. The screenshots are organized.

D8.name: Social Battery Manager
D8.desc: A two-hour reply gap is not personal. Your battery is low. Halfway through a party, your spirit quietly clocks out. Your highest form of weekend luxury is everyone agreeing to leave you alone.
D8.pro: Excellent focus and creativity when left in peace.
D8.habit: Checking the social calendar before deciding you have a sudden prior commitment.
D8.share: I got Social Battery Manager. This reply used 80% of my daily charge.

D9.name: Human Mouthpiece
D9.tagline: Saying what everyone else is thinking.
D9.desc: You say the thing the group chat will not, and boil a friend's three-day dilemma down to one line. You are not harsh, just fluent in the words everyone swallowed. Without you, gatherings feel like they are missing their interpreter.
D9.pro: Direct, and quick to unstick any conversation.
D9.habit: Drafting everyone's unspoken line, then picking the right moment to say it.
D9.share: I got Human Mouthpiece. I said the thing. Please do not be mad.

D10.name: Decluttering Assassin
D10.tagline: Throwing things away beats buying them.
D10.desc: Your wardrobe is a capsule, your apps fit one screen, and your contacts get purged every few months. Others hoard regret; you hoard empty space. Unused, unloved, untouched for three months? Out it goes.
D10.pro: A clear space and a quick, decisive mind.
D10.habit: A monthly send-off tournament where the losers are gone by morning.
D10.share: I got Decluttering Assassin. My room has an echo now.

D11.name: Midnight Emo Laureate
D11.tagline: Sunshine by day, poetry by night.
D11.desc: You are a functioning human until midnight, when the caption drafts and a photo of a streetlamp come out. You feel every small shift and can turn it into a line in three words. Your notes app holds an unpublished anthology.
D11.pro: Deep empathy and a sharp eye for feeling.
D11.habit: Re-translating last night's genius before daring to post it.
D11.share: I got Midnight Emo Laureate. Another 8,000 words written. None posted.

D12.name: Side-hustle Engine
D12.tagline: Your day job is staying alive. The hustles are extra.
D12.desc: Your resume is a chain of slashes: desk job by day, selling your photos by night, voice-over on weekends. You are not restless, you just like having more than one battery. Even a hustle that earns nothing still earns you a skill.
D12.pro: Boundless energy and a fast learning curve.
D12.habit: Three projects in progress, each one small push away from launch.
D12.share: I got Side-hustle Engine. My 47th hustle is on the way.

D13.name: Trivia Launcher
D13.tagline: Nobody asked. You still want to tell them.
D13.desc: You know octopuses have three hearts, that a banana is technically a berry, and why birds on wires never get shocked. You cannot help the "actually…" in conversation. Friends sigh, then borrow your facts to show off.
D13.pro: A wide knowledge base and delightfully odd ideas.
D13.habit: Stockpiling every fact you scroll past for a daily trivia drop.
D13.share: I got Trivia Launcher. Octopuses have three hearts. This is true.

D14.name: Emotion Organizer
D14.tagline: Filing every feeling into the right drawer.
D14.desc: Where others just feel angry, you name the exact flavour of it — offended, or afraid of being left. You label every mood and know which to air out and which to lock away. When a friend's emotions collapse, you are the first call.
D14.pro: Steady feelings and a gift for listening.
D14.habit: Tagging each day's mood before bed and filing it in your notes.
D14.share: I got Emotion Organizer. Today's mood is filed under "handled."

D15.name: Anti-hustle Pioneer
D15.tagline: You all keep grinding. I am clocking out.
D15.desc: Others work late; you shut the laptop on time. Others chase the grind; you ask whether it actually matters. You are not lazy, you just spend your effort on what counts. While they win the KPI, you win your evening back.
D15.pro: Clear boundaries and no wasted self-doubt.
D15.habit: The minute you log off becomes your own little freedom bell.
D15.share: I got Anti-hustle Pioneer. Clocking out now. Carry on.

D16.name: Digital Hoarder
D16.tagline: To save is to own. To open is to use.
D16.desc: Your bookmarks hold three thousand articles, five hundred tutorials, and two hundred "must-watch" lists. A good thing instantly becomes "save for later," and later never comes. You do not really want to read them. You just fear missing something.
D16.pro: A sharp nose for information and a complete archive.
D16.habit: Saving to "read later," where later means never.
D16.share: I got Digital Hoarder. I saved it, therefore I understood it.

questions2.text: A friend pings you "you there?" at midnight, then goes quiet. You…

options.text: Delete a thousand screenshots to calm down
Imagine what crisis they are in and get more anxious
Use the moment to finish something overdue

questions2.text: Which sounds most like your last search?

options.text: "Why do ants move before it rains"
The difference between being tired and feeling heavy

questions2.text: The gathering goes awkwardly quiet. Your first move?

options.text: Crack a joke to rescue the room
Drop a trivia fact nobody asked about
Wonder if you just said something wrong
Quietly record the moment to keep

questions2.text: That task is due tomorrow. Tonight you…

options.text: Clear your desk before you start
First figure out what this task makes you feel
Do it while filming, as future side-hustle material
Work at your own pace — no crunch, no all-nighter

questions2.text: Which compliment sounds most like you?

options.text: You always hit the nail on the head
I feel so much better after talking to you
How do you know a bit of everything

questions2.text: You see a "save this for later" post. You…

options.text: Scroll past — saved means never read
Open it to check if it is actually useful
Read it and worry you are not growing enough

fields.title: Pet Fashion Buyer
fields.skill: Knowing in three seconds whether a cat will tolerate an outfit
fields.twist: A raincoat you chose for the boss’s cat becomes a viral sensation
fields.ending: You become the mystical judge of pet fashion. The cat is still more famous
fields.comment: Your career is one long livestream, and destiny is the product
fields.share: My parallel life: Pet Fashion Buyer. You become the mystical judge of pet fashion. The cat is still more famous. What about yours?

fields.title: Meeting Mood Specialist
fields.career: Meeting minutes clerk, with a side job in atmosphere management
fields.skill: Predicting a meeting’s remaining length from a single sigh
fields.twist: The CEO discovers your Meeting Survival Guide and makes it required reading
fields.ending: You lead the new Meeting Efficiency Department. Somehow there are more meetings
fields.comment: You did not escape meetings. You turned them into your life’s work
fields.share: My parallel life: Meeting Mood Specialist. You lead the new Meeting Efficiency Department. Somehow there are more meetings. What about yours?

fields.title: Takeout Note Artist
fields.skill: Writing “less spice” so beautifully that the chef gets emotional
fields.twist: A restaurant frames your order note and becomes a local attraction
fields.ending: You open a note-writing studio. The premium service is a proposal hidden in an order
fields.comment: Other people order food to eat. You order food to leave a legacy
fields.share: My parallel life: Takeout Note Artist. You open a note-writing studio. The premium service is a proposal hidden in an order. What about yours?

fields.title: Slime Therapist
fields.skill: Understanding the emotional needs of a jelly-like creature
fields.twist: You help the Demon King’s slime, and he insists on calling you family
fields.ending: You open a slime-only practice in the castle. The fee is one sweet
fields.comment: You prove that being soft can be a solid career
fields.share: My parallel life: Slime Therapist. You open a slime-only practice in the castle. The fee is one sweet. What about yours?

fields.title: Hero Gear Inspector
fields.skill: Spotting swords that only glow to look impressive
fields.twist: You confiscate a legendary sword that does nothing but sparkle
fields.ending: Every hero visits you before a quest. You scare them more than the dragon
fields.comment: Legends are brave until quality control arrives
fields.share: My parallel life: Hero Gear Inspector. Every hero visits you before a quest. You scare them more than the dragon. What about yours?

fields.title: Dragon Delivery Dispatcher
fields.skill: Planning the most fuel-efficient fire-breathing routes
fields.twist: A dragon gives you an egg as a thank-you for a five-star shift
fields.ending: Your courier service conquers the continent. Reviews praise the perfectly warm soup
fields.comment: Other people ride dragons for status. Yours are coworkers
fields.share: My parallel life: Dragon Delivery Dispatcher. Your courier service conquers the continent. Reviews praise the perfectly warm soup. What about yours?

fields.title: AI Dream Inspector
fields.skill: Hearing a little sadness in a 404 error
fields.twist: Every AI in the city starts dreaming about the same bubble tea shop
fields.ending: You become the only human paid to read bedtime stories to machines
fields.comment: The machines have not learned love. They have learned to wait for your shift
fields.share: My parallel life: AI Dream Inspector. You become the only human paid to read bedtime stories to machines. What about yours?

fields.title: Holographic Pet Observer
fields.skill: Telling a happy digital purr from a low-battery warning
fields.twist: The electronic dogs go on strike. Their demand: actual belly rubs
fields.ending: You start a real-pet adoption movement. The hologram company names you its top rival
fields.comment: You studied artificial pets and found something real
fields.share: My parallel life: Holographic Pet Observer. You start a real-pet adoption movement. The hologram company names you its top rival. What about yours?

fields.title: Memory Organizer
fields.skill: Folding two hundred ordinary afternoons into one warm weekend
fields.twist: A client finds an extra happy memory you quietly tucked into their childhood
fields.ending: You open a memory studio, helping people put things away without losing them
fields.comment: Time moves on. You make drawers for what stays
fields.share: My parallel life: Memory Organizer. You open a memory studio, helping people put things away without losing them. What about yours?

fields.title: Inn Menu Master
fields.skill: Knowing what a table wants before anyone orders
fields.twist: Your “no scallions” order is mistaken for a secret martial arts password
fields.ending: Every clan invites you to dinner, convinced you hold an ancient menu technique
fields.comment: Where there are people, there are rivalries. Where you are, there is a menu
fields.share: My parallel life: Inn Menu Master. Every clan invites you to dinner, convinced you hold an ancient menu technique. What about yours?

fields.title: Rooftop Courier Founder
fields.skill: Delivering letters across rooftops without spilling a drop of wine
fields.twist: A family letter you deliver makes a feared sect leader cry and take three days off
fields.ending: Your courier network spans the realm: sign first, weep later
fields.comment: The fastest thing in this realm is not a sword. It is your letter
fields.share: My parallel life: Rooftop Courier Founder. Your courier network spans the realm: sign first, weep later. What about yours?

fields.title: Tall Tale Fact Checker
fields.skill: Hearing exactly where a storyteller starts making things up
fields.twist: You expose a mountain-splitting punch as stagecraft. The storyteller makes you the villain
fields.ending: Every storyteller pays you for a fact-check before opening night
fields.comment: The stories are made up. Your determination is real
fields.share: My parallel life: Tall Tale Fact Checker. Every storyteller pays you for a fact-check before opening night. What about yours?

tasks.text: Give the newest photo in your gallery a very serious movie title.
Read your last message out loud in your best newsreader voice.
Pour a glass of water, toast yourself for getting through today, then drink it.
Count the round things you can see. Write the number on the back of your hand.
Open a food app, browse a restaurant without ordering, and rate its name.
Think of someone you have not spoken to in a while. Type one thing you would say, read it, then delete it.
Hold up the nearest object for three seconds and award it Object of the Day.
Say “I am done for the day” three times. Make each one more dramatic.
Turn today’s annoyance into a news headline. Experts confirm: Monday remains shocking.
Take three slow breaths. The first word that comes to mind is your word of the day.
Look at the time and give this particular hour its own official name.
Open a book or an app’s About page. Read the first paragraph as your award acceptance speech.
Pick three useless things near you and give each a one-sentence farewell.
Take a sip of water, savor it for three seconds, and give it a rating.
Imagine everything you ate today as departments in a company. Draw up the organization chart.
Look in a mirror and give yourself three sincere compliments. “Not bad” does not count.
Describe your desk in one sentence as if you were unveiling a revolutionary new product.
Remember something that made you laugh this week. Replay it, this time in slow motion.
Give your room the name of a five-star hotel. Then reveal its actual star rating and why.
Find a song you loved ten years ago. Play just the intro and see if your body remembers.
Find this day next week on your calendar. Write one sentence to your future self.
In a private note, describe today’s weather and your current mood using one word each.
Pick an object around you, pretend it is an ancient artifact, and give it a museum caption.
Close your eyes for a minute. Identify the sounds around you and rank them by volume.
Sign your name with your non-dominant hand. Give the calligraphy a score.
Open the app you have neglected the longest. Thank it, then close it.
Give your 3 p.m. self an award. You get to invent the category.
Name three little things that did not go wrong today. A working elevator counts.
Recite today’s schedule backward, from bedtime to breakfast. Pick up the pace.
Start with “Breaking news” and report your day in fifteen seconds.

options.text: Share a good meal with someone
Keep my phone on silent all day
Go out for exactly one errand
Find a seat somewhere farther away
Put shoes on and see what happens
